endorsements.quote: Furthermore, institutions should implement silent trials, where models run in the background without influencing care.

Additionally, hospital governance boards must enforce local validation to ensure models trained on ge neral biomedical corpora perform safely within specific institutional demographics, imaging protocols and emerging FM s as Medical Devices (FMaMD) regulations.
This requires model cards that explicitly detail data provenance and known failure modes.
FMs cannot function as standalone applications; they must embed directly into existing workflows via standards such as DICOM and HL7 FHIR.
Clinical translation requires shifting the evaluation paradigm from in-silico metrics to prospective, randomized clinical trials.

Privacy can be assured through federated learning or differential privacy, 108 the robustness can be achieved by multi-institutio nal heterogeneous dataset training and posing adversarial testing to uncover the potential vulnerabilities in the model.

unlisted_practices: Implement AI-Vigilance systems, analogous to pharmacovigilance, for continuous post-deployment monitoring and auditing of AI in hospitals.
Develop regulatory certification frameworks based on formal verification and stress testing beyond clinical trial performance data.
Flag high-uncertainty AI predictions automatically for expert human review using calibrated uncertainty, with predictions below a confidence threshold mandated for human review.
Specify imaging foundation models by target population, modality, organ system, and decision context, and evaluate them under conditions reflecting clinical use.
Make value transparency explicit by stating who the model serves, what trade-offs it encodes, and how those choices are governed and updated.
Shift clinician oversight of agentic imaging AI from output verification to active process-level supervision of intermediate inference steps.
Develop foundation models through a staged pathway starting with a single modality and anatomical domain and expanding only after performance matures.
Co-design AI data and evaluation metrics with diverse stakeholders across the model lifecycle to promote inclusiveness.
Validate AI with clinical outcome measures such as time-to-diagnosis, morbidity, or altered treatment plans rather than simple accuracy scores.
Design AI user interfaces that let clinicians interrogate model reasoning by linking generated text to image regions and overlaying uncertainty maps.
Evolve reimbursement toward value-based models that incentivize certified AI systems based on demonstrated clinical and operational impact.
Use the REAL-FM paired hype and reality indicators as a checklist to evaluate foundation model claims and vendor claims before deployment.
Incorporate domain constraints such as anatomical priors, ontologies, and rule-based modules into imaging foundation models to enforce guideline-consistent reasoning.
